Okay, here's the thing. Imagine that you're sitting next to someone with a horrific, superating sore. It's just oozing pus and bleeding all over the place. What is a basic, human reaction to that?

That's right. "Oh, my God! You need to get that checked out!"

That is the EXACT SAME REACTION that people have to the obese. There is something dangerously, dreadfully wrong with your body, an obvious messed-up-ness that hits humans at an instinctual level and makes them go, "That's terrible! You need to fix that!"

Yes, it is partially revulsion, in the same way that we are instinctively revolted by injury and communicable illness and, well, poop and vomit. It's a basic survival trait to be grossed out by harmful things. That doesn't mean that people don't normally learn compassion. When someone is horrifically disfigured by an injury but we can see that it's healed, or when there's a deformity that is, well, just the way they're going to be, we can overcome the instantaneous gut-twisting reaction and go, "Oh, they're okay, that's good." This is sometimes why people call people who even definitely aren't beautiful beautiful--we want to emphasize their "okay-ness," even though some deformities and injuries make it impossible to actually be objectively, externally beautiful--like how some people have in impulse to call the mentally retarded "smart." No, if you're mentally retarded, you're by definition not "smart," but you can still be a hard worker, a nice friend, etc.

But with fat...you're not okay. The injury, such as it is, isn't being addressed. You're standing around with a huge, gaping wound and going, "I'M FINE!" when anyone with two eyeballs in their head can see the physical evidence of illness all over you. The reaction of, "Get help! That's messed up!" is one of genuine concern in the same way that saying that to someone bleeding all over the place would be sincere. And it's just as sincere as the jolt in your gut that you get when you see someone who is truly, dramatically underweight.

The FIRST THING that a doctor is trained to do is to assess you by your basic appearance, before they do any closer check ups. That's because a lot of health conditions are instantly evident. Many, many diseases are suggested to a doctor with a glance. Obesity suggests a huge number of diseases. You will ALWAYS be judged by your appearance by any competent doctor. Always. And by every human, too, because that's what humans do.
